105 likes, 1 comments - greenpointers on July 30, 2026: "The @greenpointfilmfestival (GFF) returns next week with one of its strongest international lineups yet, showcasing independent films from around the world while celebrating local filmmakers 📽️

This year’s festival, marking GFF’s 15th anniversary, will take place from August 5 to 9 at @broadwaystages (259 Green St.), where organizers are transforming a soundstage into a movie theater for the event. 

This year’s theme, Unbound, highlights films that “tell stories that challenge conventions, explore identity and present fresh perspectives,” GFF Director Anthony Argento told Greenpointers.
 
The festival will screen 130 films, including more than a dozen world premieres. The short film “The Last Goodbye”, a Polish film shot in Greenpoint, is expected to resonate deeply with local audiences. 

Nearly every screening will be followed by a filmmaker Q&A, giving audiences a chance to learn more about the creative process behind the films. GFF will also host industry panels; organizers recommend the panels on SAG-AFTRA (the union representing professionals in the industry), AI, and entertainment law and post-production.

Read the full story at greenpointers.com for more festival highlights, and you can check out the full program and grab tickets at greenpointfilmfestival.org. 

Green Pass ($150): Full fest access
Day Pass ($50)
Program rate ($20): One short + one feature 

#greenpointers #greenpointfilmfestival #greenpointfilmfestival2026 #broadwaystages".

6,091 likes, 130 comments - cultured_mag on April 18, 2026: "“Now is the moment to reframe our work as rooted in economic justice and in affordability for the worker.”

The question of the government’s investments in public art is has never been more squarely in the conversation. What projects do our governments fund, what organizations does it support, and what communities get a say? Diya Vij, the newly appointed commissioner of @nyculture, has answers—as well as experience in curation and arts administration across museums, nonprofits, and city government (notably including the Department of Cultural Affairs itself nearly a decade ago). She’s at the helm of the largest municipal funder of culture in the country, which sustains artistic communities across the five boroughs with grant funding (this February, it announced more than $74.3 million to 1,171 organizations).

In line with Mayor Mamdani’s larger goals, Vij says that affordability for artists and the city’s many cultural workers is her top priority. As an alum of Powerhouse Arts, the High Line, Creative Time, and the Queens Museum, Vij has spent decades on the ground alongside artists, curators, and other arts workers watching studio rent, materials costs, and other operating expenses skyrocket. Indeed, the city’s artist population has dropped for the first time in decades, down 4.4 percent since 2019. Supporting the arts in New York is itself an ambitious approach to economic justice.

We caught up with Vij this week to discuss her priorities for the Department of Cultural Affairs, what economic justice looks like for artists, and how to expand our idea of public art. Link in bio to read the conversation now.".

17K likes, 547 comments - nyculture on July 1, 2026: "“Our city’s artists and cultural institutions are the beating heart of New York City. … But a crushing affordability crisis has threatened to drive out the very artists who have long defined life this city. My administration is proud to make a historic, record-level investment in New York City’s arts and cultural organizations because we believe the people who make this city what it is should be able to build their lives here.” — Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani

The City’s Fiscal Year 2027 budget includes a historic $323.8 million for @NYCulture—the highest-ever appropriation of funding for arts and culture in NYC! 🙌

For the first time, the budget includes a Cultural Stability Fund to support struggling arts organizations. The initiative provides a $10 million annual pool through fiscal year 2029, serving as an emergency resource for cultural organizations and artists.

“At a time when artists and cultural organizations have been asked to do more with less, this budget says something powerful: New York believes in the arts and in its artists. Arts and culture are how we tell our stories, care for one another, and shape the future of this city. I’m incredibly proud that we’re choosing to stand with the people who make New York the creative capital of the world.” — NYC Cultural Affairs Commissioner Diya Vij

Visit the link in our bio to read Isa Farfan’s full article in @Hyperallergic.

#NYCulture #NYC".
